name: Question 14
problem: Consider a thin rod along the $x$-axis over the interval $0\le x\le 4$ whose mass density function is $\lambda (x)=\sqrt{x}.$ Find the $x$-coordinate of the center of mass of the rod.
worked_solution:
The center of mass of a rod placed along the $x$-axis over the interval $a\le x\le b$ whose mass density function is $\lambda (x)$ is given by 

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m},
$$

 

where 

- $m={\int }_{a}^{b}\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x$ is the mass of the rod,

- ${M}_{O}={\int }_{a}^{b}\,x\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x$ is the moment of the rod about the origin $O.$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=\sqrt{x},\,a=0,\,b=4.
$$

So, the mass of the rod is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\int }_{0}^{4}\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{x}^{1/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3/2}]}_{0}^{4} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot {4}^{3/2}-0 \\  & =\frac{16}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the moment of the rod about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{0}^{4}x\cdot \sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{x}^{3/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{2}{5}{x}^{5/2}]}_{0}^{4} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}\cdot {4}^{5/2}-0 \\  & =\frac{64}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m}=\frac{(\frac{64}{5})}{(\frac{16}{3})}=\frac{12}{5}.
$$

Question 14

Consider a thin rod along the x-axis over the interval 0≤x≤4 whose mass density function is λ(x)=x. Find the x-coordinate of the center of mass of the rod.

a
125
b
163
c
323
d
165
e
645
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The center of mass of a rod placed along the x-axis over the interval a≤x≤b whose mass density function is λ(x) is given by

x―=MOm,

where

  • m=∫abλ(x)dx is the mass of the rod,

  • MO=∫abxλ(x)dx is the moment of the rod about the origin O.

In our case, we have

λ(x)=x,a=0,b=4.

So, the mass of the rod is

m=∫04xdx=∫04x1/2dx=[23x3/2]04=23⋅43/2−0=163

and the moment of the rod about the origin is

MO=∫04x⋅xdx=∫04x3/2dx=[25x5/2]04=25⋅45/2−0=645.

Therefore,

x―=MOm=(645)(163)=125.
